title: Australia signs deal to join Horizon Europe's Pillar II
dek: Australian organisations will be able to join and lead Pillar II consortia, with transitional access to calls from January 2027.
key_facts: Horizon Europe Pillar II, worth €52.4 billion
In Brussels, by Commissioner Ekaterina Zaharieva and Minister Tim Ayres
From January 2027 for Pillar II calls
Expected by mid-2027, after Australian parliamentary scrutiny
body: The EU and Australia have signed an agreement that associates Australia to Pillar II of Horizon Europe, the part of the programme that funds collaborative research in fields such as health, climate, energy and digital technologies. Pillar II is worth €52.4 billion. Commissioner for Startups, Research and Innovation Ekaterina Zaharieva and Australia's Minister for Industry and Innovation and Minister for Science, Tim Ayres, signed the text in Brussels.

Under the agreement, Australian researchers and organisations can join and lead international consortia and receive funding on terms similar to those of EU participants. For the rest of the programme nothing changes: Australians keep their access to the parts of the Excellent Science pillar open to non-EU countries, such as the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions, and to the Innovative Europe pillar, depending on the conditions of each call.

Transitional arrangements apply from January 2027. From then, Australian entities can apply to Pillar II calls and be evaluated as prospective beneficiaries. The Commission expects the association to be formally completed by mid-2027, once Australia's parliament has scrutinised it. Negotiations had concluded in June 2026, and Australia is now the 24th country associated with Horizon Europe.
why: Ullswater Investments analysis: for consortia preparing Pillar II proposals for the 2027 calls, Australian universities, research organisations and companies become partners that can be funded and even lead projects. That makes it easier to add complementary expertise from outside Europe. Because the arrangements are transitional until the association is formally completed, coordinators should check the eligibility wording of each call and keep in close contact with Australian partners as the process moves forward.
